summary: myseliasan's fleet control plane gains a consolidated Notifications page (badged nav item under a new System group) that lists its own events plus every event a managed node pushes up its control channel, with unread/all + per-node source filters, infinite scroll, live SSE updates, and an Acknowledge action that marks the notification read (new POST /api/notifications/{id}/read) and propagates AI-detection acknowledgements back to the source node alert over the proxy. The Nodes page gains a pop-up Adopt dialog (from a discovered node or a manual-entry button, for nodes outside multicast range) and a tabbed node Settings modal (Details/Camera Health/Users/Backup & Recovery/Version & Health) styled like mymatasan's own Settings page, all tunneled over the node proxy; Details edits the node's operator-facing name/description/icon via a new PUT /api/nodes/{id}, and Version & Health mirrors mymatasan's software version, update check/apply, and live service health/readiness plus host CPU/mem/disk. Each adopted node also gets a Wipe action that remotely factory-resets it (mirroring mymatasan's own secure wipe) behind an allowReset gate check and an auto-proceeding confirmation countdown. The cross-node Live Views wall was rebuilt for full parity with mymatasan's own Live Views: grid layout picker, pagination, fullscreen, drag-to-reorder tiles, per-tile maximize and PTZ, and an in-wall cross-node Add-camera picker. Per-node device access levels were renamed viewer/superadmin to viewer/admin throughout the RBAC UI and API docs to avoid confusion with RBAC's own superadmin role; Users/Roles admin tables gained pagination, and Roles gained Rename + Refresh. Side-nav: Live Views moved above the Nodes tree, both tree levels now expand/collapse on double-click, and the nav list area scrolls independently of the fixed header/footer chrome. Underlying this, the shared apphost runtime (infra/apphost/run.go) now mirrors the root /ready readiness probe under /api/ready on every app, since a reverse control tunnel like myseliasan's only dispatches against the /api subrouter and could not reach the root path — this is what powers the Version & Health tab's readiness pill and requires managed mymatasan nodes to be rebuilt to expose it.
compatibility: No database schema changes; ManagedNode's existing Name/Description/Icon fields (added in a prior release) are reused by the new PUT /api/nodes/{id} endpoint. Existing myseliasan installs gain the Notifications nav item, node Settings dialog, Wipe button, and rebuilt Live Views wall automatically after upgrade with no config changes. The Version & Health tab's readiness pill and any control-tunnel feature relying on /api/ready require the adopted mymatasan node to be rebuilt/upgraded to a build that serves it; an older node simply shows the readiness pill as unavailable rather than failing the panel, and all other tabs are unaffected. The node Wipe action is a destructive, opt-in operation gated by the target node's own bootstrap.allowReset config (default-safe) and a confirmation countdown before it proceeds.
